list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT host FROM host_sample ORDER BY host

panels.title: CPU by class (runner / agent / other), per host
panels.description: Sum of per-process CPU for each attribution class. Every class is a direct sum of its own processes; 'other' is not a residual.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval),
  host || ' ' || class AS metric,
  AVG(cpu_pct) AS value
FROM class_sample
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host IN ($host)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Host CPU %
panels.description: The host's own CPU counter (top / /proc/stat), independent of the per-process sums above.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval),
  host AS metric,
  AVG(cpu_pct) AS value
FROM host_sample
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host IN ($host)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Host memory used
panels.description: Memory in use (MemTotal − MemAvailable on Linux; hw.memsize − free pages on macOS).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(ts, $__interval),
  host AS metric,
  AVG(mem_used_mb) AS value
FROM host_sample
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host IN ($host)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Pre-start latency, entry-point jobs, by executing-runner labels
panels.description: started_at − created_at for jobs with no `needs:` dependency — where it equals runner-availability wait. Empty until the poller is given a needs resolver (is_entry_point is NULL until then); see the table below for the unrestricted number.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '1h'),
  labels AS metric,
  AVG(pre_start_latency_seconds) AS value
FROM job_event
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND is_entry_point = 1 AND pre_start_latency_seconds IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Pre-start latency by executing-runner labels (all jobs in range)
panels.description: started_at − created_at for every job. For a job with `needs:` this includes time blocked on upstream jobs, so it is an upper bound on runner-availability wait. Labels are the executing runner's, not the job's runs-on.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  labels,
  COUNT(pre_start_latency_seconds) AS jobs,
  ROUND(AVG(pre_start_latency_seconds)::numeric, 1) AS avg_seconds,
  ROUND((PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY pre_start_latency_seconds))::numeric, 1) AS p95_seconds,
  ROUND(MAX(pre_start_latency_seconds)::numeric, 1) AS max_seconds
FROM job_event
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND pre_start_latency_seconds IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY labels
ORDER BY avg_seconds DESC

panels.title: Runner busy time (from job windows)
panels.description: Sum of [started_at, completed_at] per runner over the selected range, as hours and as a share of the range. Utilization per runner, computed from GitHub's job records rather than host sampling.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  runner_name,
  COUNT(*) AS jobs,
  ROUND(SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (completed_at - started_at)))::numeric / 3600, 2) AS busy_hours,
  ROUND(100 * SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (completed_at - started_at)))::numeric
        / GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ($__timeTo()::timestamptz - $__timeFrom()::timestamptz)), 1), 1) AS utilization_pct
FROM job_event
WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND runner_name <> '' AND started_at IS NOT NULL AND completed_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY runner_name
ORDER BY busy_hours DESC

panels.title: Where CI time goes: step durations
panels.description: Average and total duration per step name across every job in the range. If most wall-clock is in the build step, more runners help less than caching would.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  s.name AS step,
  COUNT(*) AS runs,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.completed_at - s.started_at)))::numeric, 1) AS avg_seconds,
  ROUND(SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.completed_at - s.started_at)))::numeric / 3600, 2) AS total_hours
FROM job_step s
JOIN job_event j ON j.job_id = s.job_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(j.created_at) AND s.started_at IS NOT NULL AND s.completed_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.name
ORDER BY total_hours DESC
LIMIT 25
